newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Cariparma plans share offer -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Cariparma plans share offer -- paper.

text.p: Italian savings bank Cassa di Risparmio di Parma e Piacenza (Cariparma) plans a share offer next year of up to 2 trillion lire and to list on the Milan bourse, Il Sole newspaper said on Sunday.

Il Sole quoted Cariparma chairman Luciano Silingardi as saying "privatisation is now in the stocks and we are speeding up even though we are waiting for the definitive text of legislation on banking foundations."
Silingardi said the placement, which would also include strategic alliances, was being brought forward a year from 1999 as originally planned.
Cariparma savings bank is 51.6 percent controlled by the Cariparma foundation and 20.7 percent controlled by the Cassa Piacenza foundation.
The rest is held by around 25,000 shareholders, but is not quoted, Il Sole said.
"With Merrill Lynch, which is assisting us, we aim to lower our stake to 30 percent, putting a total 40 percent up for sale," Silingardi said.
He said it was early to say how much the expected amount on offer would be.
"Let's say on the basis of the last few balance sheets, the package could be estimated at around 1.2 trillion lire. But the placement could be of larger dimensions," he said.
He did not rule out a capital increase. "It's certainly an idea. Entering the stock market can justify an operation which reinforces the bank for further developments," he said.
"And I'm increasingly of the opinion that Cariparma could ask the markets for up to 2.0 trillion in one fell swoop," he said.

He added it was in the interest of the bank to remain under the control of a stable core of businesses from Parma, Piacenza and Lombardy, although its independence could be strengthened by strategic alliances with other banks, insurers and financial service providers.
As for a private placement alongside a public offer, Silingardi said they would look at investors useful to the bank's strategy who did not question its independence.
Cariparma made a net profit of 106 billion lire in 1996, up 12 percent on the previous year and equal to a return on equity of 6.5 percent.
